subject: Deal structuring: commit velocity vouchers & reseller split
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@greengrid.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenGrid Procurement <procurement@greengrid.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer — pricing boundaries and reseller margin ask

Connor / Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. GreenGrid is preparing an internal justification for a 24‑month private offer on AWS. A few quick asks so we can move to procurement: 

- Can Redwood support an initial list‑price anchor that’s 40% above the committed effective rate so we can preserve internal discounting cadence?
- We need a clear passback to our reseller partners — what margin waterfall would you support for an MSP channel where the reseller needs a 12–15% net margin?
- On commit velocity: Procurement wants a voucher mechanism (one‑time credits applied to spike months) rather than a strict daily metering credit. Do you have experience packaging that in the private offer flow?

Attachments: sample PO template (not sent here).

Goal is to have a binding commercial term sheet by EOD Wednesday. Can you send a couple of packaging options (list anchor + voucher split + reseller split) and the preferred invoice routing?

Best,
Susan Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | GreenGrid
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@greengrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — pricing boundaries and reseller margin ask

Susan — thanks, this is clear and helpful. I put together three packaging options and a short note on how we typically operationalize vouchers for commit velocity. Summary here; full spreadsheet attached.

Option A — Anchor + Standard Reseller Passback
- Effective committed rate (24mo): $0.028/token
- List anchor: $0.047/token (~68% above committed) to preserve internal discount waterfall
- Reseller net margin: 12% applied as passback to the MSP at invoice time (sales credit routing)
- Voucher approach: 1x quarterly voucher pool (applied to invoice month of spike). Vouchers are issued as a billing credit line item; they don’t change list price.

Option B — Higher Anchor, Tiered Reseller Split
- Effective rate: $0.030/token
- List anchor: $0.060/token (~100% above committed) for more negotiation room
- Reseller margin: tiered (12% up to $1.5M, 15% thereafter). We recommend this if you need progressive reseller economics.
- Voucher approach: monthly velocity vouchers sized to forecast variance (smaller pulses, auto‑apply when monthly consumption > forecast * 1.2).

Option C — Conservative Anchor + Guaranteed MSP Floor
- Effective rate: $0.026/token
- List anchor: $0.038/token (~46% above committed)
- Reseller margin: guaranteed floor of 12% with an overage share (Redwood pays 50% of any reserve draw to the reseller beyond the floor for the first year)
- Voucher approach: annual voucher pool that can be split between months via a self‑service portal — simpler legal packaging but larger single credit line.

Notes on implementation:
- AWS private offer allows list price + discounted price mapping; we can push the voucher as a separate credit mechanism tracked off‑invoice (billing credit) so it doesn’t affect the AWS SKU mapping.
- For reseller passback, we normally produce a monthly reconciliation CSV and can integrate with your reseller’s invoicing system. Naomi will handle the ops template.

I attached a pricing workbook with per‑month examples and sample language for the PO and invoice routing. My ask: pick A/B/C or ask for a hybrid by tomorrow EOD and we’ll lock the SOW and produce a private offer draft.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-proposed-pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx, vendor-sla-draft.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@greengrid.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — pricing boundaries and reseller margin ask

Small ops notes from my side (copied Naomi for reconciliation):

- Reseller margin mechanics: we recommend passing on the margin as a single line 'MSP passback' on Redwood invoices to the bill‑to entity. If GreenGrid wants the reseller to receive funds directly, we can set up a broker fee disbursement but that increases accounting complexity and requires a short addendum.
- Voucher accounting: treating vouchers as contra‑revenue line items keeps marketplace reporting intact (list vs committed) and avoids touching usage metering. That also makes it easier to audit in SOC2 reports.
- Tax handling: reseller passbacks should be modeled net of VAT in EU scenarios; for the US it’s simpler but check your AR team if you need reseller‑facing invoices.

Operational ask: Naomi, can you produce the reconciliation CSV template and confirm lead times for a private‑offer activation on AWS once paperwork's signed?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Susan Park <susan@greengrid.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenGrid Procurement <procurement@greengrid.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — pricing boundaries and reseller margin ask

Connor / Ben / Naomi — appreciate the options and the spreadsheet. We reviewed with execs and prefer Option B (higher anchor + tiered reseller split). A few follow ups before we sign: 

1) Can Redwood commit to 5 business days SLA for voucher issuance after a request (our procurement needs the ability to apply credits quickly if usage spikes)?
2) Confirm the reseller tier breakpoints (12% up to $1.5M, 15% thereafter) are calculated on Redwood net revenue, not GreenGrid gross spend.
3) Please produce the AWS private offer draft (mapping of SKU to list price + committed mapping) and a short addendum covering voucher handling and reconciliation cadence.

If we get those items by Friday EOD, procurement will circulate the PO and legal will do a fast review. HubSpot shows the deal as 'contracting' (GG-1247).

Next steps: Connor — we are happy to sign once the private offer draft and voucher SLA language are in.

Best regards,
Susan Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | GreenGrid
